summary:
We trained or started about 20 models of our own. Only one of them ever reached a final with a private gain: the DaughterNet v1 division insertion. It cost under 1 GPU-hour on Kaggle (about 20 minutes of training on 2xT4) and about 7 hours of wall time from the plan to the LB submission (23 Sep 20:30 to 24 Sep 03:45 UTC). It was also the only model validated on held-out videos, with 5 folds and the 44b6 leak groups kept whole. It read +0.001 public and +0.005/+0.003/+0.003 private in three clean pairs. Everything else fell into three groups:
(a) The model itself was weak. Friend A's from-scratch detector scored 0.68 on the unseen embryo against 0.88 for pilkwang, and as the secondary it read -0.025 public / -0.014 private. Other examples are the dorado-trained DaughterNet (AUC 0.62), DaughterNet v2, and the exp04/05/14 recipes.
(b) It was judged in-sample and then closed or kept on public reads. Examples are the exp03B/exp08/exp16/exp17/exp23 fine-tunes on hold12, and SEC n2a on 4 dummy train clips. Two of them (secondary exp23, secondary weight 0.5) were in fact private-positive (+0.003, +0.007) and were discarded on public reads.
(c) It was never finished for lack of people, disk or compute. Examples are the dense-label teacher, friend B's GBM division ranker (paused at 148/199 videos), friend A's full-res DaughterNet-B (lost to a PC reboot), the appearance-aware linker (blocked: needs leak-free init), and a detector retrain (declined at ~23 h per run on the 5070 Ti).
The pattern that made the team stop trusting its own models started on 6 Sep. The clean pipeline scored 0.990 on hold12 but 0.899 on the LB. The post-mortem concluded that 'LB is the only trustworthy signal' and 'stop spending GPU on fine-tune variants' (CONTEXT l.242-252). It correctly saw that pilkwang weights make every train-clip lab in-sample. But the fix, an honest held-out validator, never materialised: friend A's scratch validator stalled at 0.68 against a 0.85 gate. So the team moved to forking public notebooks and reading the public LB. Five model swaps then read negative on public. That '0 of 5' record (FACTS F-TRN-41) became a prior and then the R9 rule 'no detector/edge/head retraining before 29 Sep', set on 25 Sep. On private, those five swaps were 1 up, 2 flat and 2 down, not 0 of 5. The first model with honest folds was started only on 23 Sep, 20 days after our first submission, and it was the one that transferred.
On time: the records show that learned downstream models on the public detector are cheap. A division model, edge or division re-ranking, or a coordinate head costs 0.3-7 GPU-hours plus 1-3 days of engineering each, which fit easily into 20 days. The expensive item is a detector retrain: ~23 h per run on the 5070 Ti, 1.3-2.1 h per epoch on a T4. That needed week-1 planning and was feasible only on friend A's GPU or the pooled Kaggle quotas of three accounts. Only one account's quota was used; the two teammates' ~30 h/week each sat idle.

summary: Short answer: the route was feasible inside our ~20 working days and it did not need a new detector. What stopped us was an early wrong turn, not a lack of compute. On 6 Sep, probe 1 (0.899) showed that our local numbers were in-sample. We concluded from it that 'the LB is the only trustworthy signal' (CONTEXT l.242-245) and switched to a public notebook plus one knob per probe. The only honest validator we then considered was a detector trained from scratch, the most expensive piece. It stalled at LOEO 0.68 (l.507-515) and cost −0.025 as a secondary (probe 10, l.267-274), so trained models as a whole were demoted on 10 Sep (l.496-500). The cheap alternative is what ymg_aq (#18) did: keep the public detector, cache its candidate graph for all 199 videos, and train light heads with embryo-wise CV. It needs about 2–4 person-days for the harness plus ~10 GPU-h. We only assembled it on 19–23 Sep. The one head we built on it, DaughterNet, took about 1 day and under 1 GPU-h, and it is the only lever that transferred (+0.003…+0.005 private). Before then, early GBM division rankers had too few positives on 12–48 videos (A8 l.163; B20 l.1017), the 199-video table was blocked by the 82 GB of data and friend B leaving on 18 Sep, 12 days had no submissions, and from 25 Sep rule R9 banned any retraining (DECISIONS l.1814). My estimates for our resources: (d) harness alone 3–5 person-days, about +0.000…+0.003 private. (a) GBM edge/division/coordinate heads 10–15 person-days, 10–20 GPU-h, about +0.005…+0.020. (b) Corwin-style stages 12–20 person-days, about +0.004…+0.012. (c) own 2.5D detector + LP 25–40 person-days and 60–150+ GPU-h, not feasible end to end in 20 days, outcome −0.02…+0.02. A 20-day plan with heads first, built on (d) then (a), would plausibly have reached private ~0.925–0.940 (central ~0.930) instead of 0.920. That means silver was likely (cut 0.921–0.924) and gold unlikely (0.941). This is uncertain: only two training embryos, a private embryo that is sparser, 151 divisions, our own failed cross-embryo coordinate retrain, and the leaders' unknown preparation time.

summary: The records show that training our own models was not skipped. It was done in two short bursts, and the stretch between them was mostly empty. Burst 1 ran 5-9 Sep: 1200-iteration fine-tunes of the pilkwang weights (exp03-exp17) on Kaggle, plus friend A's from-scratch runs on his 5070 Ti. Friend A's runs were 5 and then 20 epochs on 6bba only (6bba->44b6 LOEO), and 21+10 epochs on all 199 videos. Burst 2 ran 23-24 Sep: DaughterNet v1/v2, which was trained in about 20-25 min on Kaggle and is the only lever that carried over to private, plus a dorado-pretrained variant and a coordinate-head retrain. A small burst 3 on 27 Sep was the SEC secondary fine-tunes (exp71 and exp77, about 2.1 h and 2.4 h). Between 10 and 22 Sep no model was trained except friend A's AdaBN test and ranker prototypes. That window holds 5.6 of our 5.6 idle days and most of the 12 days with no submission. By my estimate (fractions of each day's main team effort, 27 days from 3 to 29 Sep), the split is: (a) own training/building about 5.7 days, (b) porting public notebooks about 2.9, (c) knob tuning and public probes about 4.8, (d) research rounds, rules and planning about 6.2, (e) ops and infrastructure about 2.0, (f) idle about 5.6. At each decision point training was dropped for a reason recorded at the time, and the GPU quota was never one of them. The reasons were: local validation is leaky, so the LB was made the only judge (6 Sep). Our first own models lost on the LB (scratch secondary 0.920, exp23 0.937) and our LOEO model plateaued at 0.68 (8-9 Sep). A public TTA stack absorbed the fine-tune gain (10-11 Sep). Teammates were unavailable: friend A was silent 10-18 Sep, and friend B worked effectively one day (15 Sep), was blocked by disk and was gone by 18 Sep. Public shortcuts arrived (DivNet 18 Sep, x138 24 Sep). A detector retrain was declined 'on arithmetic' (24 Sep), and the plan pre-registered a ban on retraining (R9, 25 Sep). That ban plus a permission block delayed the only retrain by about 13 h (26-27 Sep). The user's public-rank targets (0.950 and 0.97 on 22 Sep, 'aggressive mode' on 27 Sep) pushed the last week into knob ladders. Claude token limits paused research on 12-13 Sep and 24 Sep.

summary: GPU was never the binding constraint. The records show spare compute in every week and on every machine. Our own Kaggle quota went mostly to probe and dummy kernels: about 25 of 30 h in week 1, about 19 of 30 h in week 3 with 26.7 h still free on 23 Sep, and about 27 of 30 h in 26-29 Sep. Only about 20-25 GPU-h of the whole month went to training anything. The teammates' two quotas (about 30 h/week each, about 200 h in total) were effectively unused; they were offered only on 28 Sep. Friend A's RTX 5070 Ti delivered about 36 GPU-h of training, all between 6 and 9 Sep. That run reproduced the pilkwang recipe from scratch on sparse labels and gave LOEO 0.68, and 0.920 public / 0.893 private as a secondary. After that the card sat idle 10-18 Sep and again after 24 Sep. Friend B contributed about one day of CPU work (15 Sep) and no training; he was out from 18 Sep. Friend C was friend A's own Mac, and nothing ran on it. The one learned model that paid off on private (DaughterNet, +0.003..+0.005) took about 28 GPU-minutes and one evening, 23 Sep 18:30 to 24 Sep 03:45 UTC. Our own 25 Sep report priced the top-team path at at least 2-3 weeks and 50-100 GPU-h. We had roughly 150-300+ realistically usable GPU-h, so compute covered that path 2-5 times over. The person-days were the tight part: the lead had about 15 active days and friend A about 12, and a focused own-model line needs one person for 2-3 weeks. The binding constraints were: (1) no honest validation bed for learned models until 23-24 Sep, because the pilkwang weights are in-sample on all 199 videos; (2) the owner of the only local GPU was absent at the decision points; (3) explicit decisions that ruled out retraining: 'fine-tuned primaries closed' on 11-12 Sep, 'detector retrain declined on arithmetic' on 24 Sep, and PRE-REGISTRATION v3 on 25 Sep (M3 = NO, no retraining before 29 Sep); (4) the 7-10 h scoring latency and the 12 h runtime limit made every model-side LB read cost a day and made heavy extra inference risky. Knob probes were cheap by comparison. Realistically, starting about 11 Sep with a one-night leak-group CV bed, 15-17 days and about 150+ GPU-h were available. That was enough for 2-3 small learned components (divisions, edge rerank, localisation) and one or two sparse-label detector fine-tunes. A converged own detector ensemble like yu4u's was at the edge of feasible and would have needed friend A's card full-time.
